(analogy) Queries, keys, and values are all vectors that participate in a single attention step. Queries represent what a token is looking for, keys represent what each candidate token offers, and values carry the information [1]. The query is compared to each key to determine how much attention should be paid to the corresponding value.

## A worked example

Imagine you're searching for information about "cats." Your query might be a vector representing "cats." Each document in a database has a key vector representing its topic. The dot product of your "cats" query and each document's key vector tells you how relevant that document is to your search. The value vector for each document contains the actual text of the document.
